items.title: Every Dog and Cat at Mississauga's Shelter Is $25 to Adopt This Month, Vaccines Included
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga Animal Services has launched a two-week Homeward Bound adoption event after its shelter reached capacity for dogs, cutting the adoption fee for any dog or cat to $25 plus HST and applicable licensing fees from August 8 to August 22. That's a steep discount from the shelter's usual rates, which typically run $280 plus HST for dogs and puppies and up to $190 plus HST for cats and kittens. INsauga reports the event is open to anyone looking to add a pet, no appointment is required, and adopters must be at least 18 years old, though wait times may vary given the expected demand. Every animal adopted through the shelter has already received basic medical care, including vaccinations and spay or neuter surgery, which helps offset some of the costs new owners would otherwise face right away. Shelter staff are also available to guide first-time pet owners through training, feeding and exercise, and to help a newly adopted animal settle into its new home. City officials say the goal is simple: every adoption frees up space for another animal still waiting for a home.

items.title: Credit Valley Conservation Warns of Dangerous Urban Streams as Storms Soak the Region Through Saturday
items.summary: According to INsauga, Credit Valley Conservation issued a flood outlook statement Thursday covering Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon that remains in effect through Sunday. The agency says thunderstorms carrying peak rainfall of 30 to 40 millimetres per hour are possible both Friday and Saturday, with Environment and Climate Change Canada forecasting localized storms across the entire Credit River watershed starting Friday morning and continuing into Saturday evening. CVC reports the upper and middle sections of the watershed had already picked up roughly 20 to 30 millimetres of localized rainfall as of Thursday evening. While the agency says it does not expect the Credit River or its major tributaries to flood outright, it is warning of possible localized flash flooding and water pooling on roads and in low-lying urban areas. CVC cautions that urban streams and rivers can become especially dangerous near culverts, bridges and dams during heavy rain events. Residents are being told to stay away from all watercourses and to keep children and pets clear of moving water through the weekend.

items.title: After a Failed Provincial Bid, Bonnie Crombie Wants Her Old Mississauga Job Back
items.summary: According to INsauga, Bonnie Crombie is campaigning to reclaim the Mississauga mayor's seat she gave up in January 2024, when she left to lead the Ontario Liberal Party after winning its leadership race the previous month. Residents will decide her fate at the polls on October 26, and Crombie told INsauga in an interview this week that she knows some voters may question her commitment given how she left, but argues she's now better prepared for the job than before. She described coming back with more experience and seasoning, saying her time observing the problems facing Ontario municipalities as provincial Liberal leader taught her what works and what doesn't on issues like affordable housing and rising crime. Her provincial detour did not go as planned. The Liberals were decisively defeated by Doug Ford's Progressive Conservatives in the February 2025 election, and Crombie herself lost her bid for the Mississauga East-Cooksville riding before formally stepping down as Liberal leader in January 2026. INsauga reports she first signalled she wouldn't rule out another mayoral run in late 2025, months after her political career appeared to stall. Crombie had served as Mississauga's mayor for a decade before stepping down, having succeeded her mentor Hazel McCallion in 2014.

items.title: 43 Highway Closures Hit Peel Region's Busiest Routes on August 7
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the province has scheduled 43 separate closures across provincial highways in Peel Region for August 7, 2026. The affected routes include Highway 10, Highway 401, Highway 403, Highway 410, Highway 9 and the Queen Elizabeth Way, six of the busiest corridors linking Mississauga to the rest of the Greater Toronto Area. Mississauga.com reports the closures are tied to short-term and emergency repairs and general maintenance work rather than one large construction project. With so many highways affected on the same day, drivers are advised to plan their trip before heading out rather than assume their usual route will be clear. The outlet also points to a separate closure list for anyone travelling to highways outside Peel Region. Commuters passing through the region on Friday should expect at least some detours or lane restrictions as crews work through the scheduled repairs.

items.title: The Officer Who Ran Onto a Burning Plane at Pearson Is Getting a Street Named After Him
items.summary: According to INsauga, a street dedication ceremony this month will honour retired Sgt. Lonsdale “Lonny” Blackett, who became the first Black police officer in Brampton and Mississauga after joining Peel Regional Police's very first recruiting class in 1974. He was one of two Black recruits in that class and the only one to complete training, going on to a 33-year career during which he faced racism both on and off the force before eventually becoming a recruiter who helped bring in other minority officers. Blackett also helped found the Peel Regional Police Airport Division, and INsauga reports he was one of the officers who ran onto the burning wreckage of Air France Flight 358 to help evacuate people after it crashed at Pearson International Airport in 2005. All 309 passengers and crew aboard survived, and Blackett received a commendation for his role in the rescue. The City of Brampton began the process of naming a street after him in February, and the upcoming ceremony will mark the future site of Lonsdale Blackett Way at Mississauga Road just south of Bovaird Drive West. Since the street itself has not been built yet as part of planned development in the area, the city says the event will be a ceremonial dedication rather than an unveiling of a finished road. Residents are invited to attend, though the city notes parking will be limited.

items.title: After a Burst Pipe and a Food Truck Detour, Pal' Antojo Finally Opens on Queen Street
items.summary: According to INsauga, Pal' Antojo Mexican Restaurant has officially opened at 277 Queen St. S. in Mississauga, taking over a space that Border MX Mexican Grill quietly vacated late last year. Border MX had operated there since 2014 and built a following for its open-air patio, live music nights and mix of traditional and modern Mexican dishes, but the business hit trouble after a pipe burst inside the restaurant on Valentine's Day 2025, causing major water damage to the kitchen. INsauga reports the restaurant reopened that April before eventually closing for good. Pal' Antojo said in May that it was preparing the same Queen Street location to open, running a food truck behind the building in the meantime to keep serving customers. The restaurant announced it was finally open with the message “The wait is over!” The opening gives the block a new tenant after months of uncertainty following Border MX's closure.
